newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares hit three-month low.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares hit three-month low.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell to three-month lows in paltry trade on Monday, weighed down by gloom over poor 1996 results by smaller firms and by a number of shares going ex-dividend.

The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.24 percent to 151.78 points, its lowest level since January 4, after shares worth just 346,000 dinars ($489,000) changed hands. It was the third consecutive daily fall in the index.
Brokers said poor results by food producers and industrial firms, badly hit by a cut in Jordan's 1996 trade protocol with sanction-hit Iraq, continued to depress some stocks.

Vegetable oil producer Universal Modern Industries, which reported a sharp fall in 1996 profits, fell by the five percent daily maximum for a second day running, dropping to 0.08 dinars to 1.42 dinars.

Jordan French Insurance, which brokers said had announced net 1996 profit of 586,000 dinars from 755,000 in 1995, also fell five percent 1.85 dinars. Monday's sole transaction of 200 shares was the first in the stock since it went ex-dividend on Saturday.

Two other insurance firms which have yet to announce results both fell five percent on fears over their performance in 1996, brokers said. Arab International Union Insurance and National Ahlia Insurance fell to 2.18 dinars and 2.66 dinars respectively, both falling in just a single trade.
Jordan Electric Power which announced a 0.1 dinar dividend, fought the downward trend, gaining 0.06 dinars to 1.71 dinars in Monday's busiest trade, worth nearly 84,000 dinars.

But falling shares dominated on Monday, led by the heavyweight Arab Bank which went ex-dividend on Saturday after an AGM at which it declined to set a date for a long-expected bonus share issue. It fell one dinar to 252 dinars.
Losing stocks outnumbered gainers by 21 to 11, with another six trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-perfoming shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.23 percent to 79.59 points, 4.56 percent down from the start of the year.
